drivingQuestion: Which portion of the sciatic nerve did bar Peyoli remove and leave, and in accordance with whose opinion had he been instructed?
outcomeNote: Rav Sheshet's statement is reformulated so that the instructor's ruling matches R' Yehuda, for whom the remainder is permitted even rabbinically.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ בַּר פָּיוֹלֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, וְקָא מְנַקַּר אַטְמָא. הֲוָה קָא גָאֵים לֵיהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חוֹת בֵּיהּ טְפֵי, הַשְׁתָּא לָא חֲזֵיתָךְ – סְפֵית לִי אִיסּוּרָא!
segments.en: «GEMARA:» A man known as «bar Peyoli was standing before Shmuel and was removing» the sciatic nerve from the «leg» of an animal. «He was cutting» out the nerve without scraping away the surrounding flesh, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda. Shmuel «said to him: Go down further» and scrape away the flesh in order to remove the entire nerve. «Now,» if I would «not have seen you» and instructed you in the process of removing the sciatic nerve, «you would have fed me forbidden» meat.

segments.he: אִירְתַת, נְפַל סַכִּינָא מִידֵיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא תִּירְתַת, דְּאוֹרִי לָךְ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹרִי לָךְ.
segments.en: Bar Peyoli became «afraid» due to Shmuel’s rebuke and «the knife fell from his hand.» Shmuel «said to him: Do not be afraid.» I do not think that you are an ignoramus or a wicked person. You are removing the sciatic nerve as you were taught; the person «who taught you» must hold «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda,» and this is how «he taught you» to remove the sciatic nerve. But I hold that the entire sciatic nerve must be removed, in accordance with the opinion of the first tanna.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַאי דִּשְׁקַל בַּר פָּיוֹלֵי – דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה. מִכְּלָל דְּשַׁיַּיר – דְּרַבָּנַן, לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה. אֶלָּא, דְּאוֹרִי לֵיהּ כְּמַאן אוֹרִי לֵיהּ?
segments.en: «Rav Sheshet said» in explanation of this incident: «That which bar Peyoli removed was» the section of the sciatic nerve one is required to remove «by Torah law according to» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda.» The Gemara asks: Based upon this statement, one can derive «by inference that he left» behind the section of the sciatic nerve one is required to remove «by rabbinic law according to» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda. But» if so, «in accordance with whose» opinion did the person «who taught him» how to remove the sciatic nerve «teach him?» Even according to Rabbi Yehuda he would have transgressed a rabbinic prohibition.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַאי דִּשְׁקַל בַּר פָּיוֹלֵי – דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וּמַאי דְּשַׁיַּיר – דְּרַבָּנַן, לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר; דְּאִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – אֲפִילּוּ מִדְּרַבָּנַן שְׁרֵי.
segments.en: «Rather, Rav Sheshet said: That which bar Peyoli removed» was the section of the sciatic nerve that is forbidden «by Torah law. And that which he left» over is forbidden «by rabbinic law according to» the opinion of «Rabbi Meir,» as explained above (92b) in a baraita; «as if» one were to follow the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda,» the section that bar Peyoli left over «is permitted even by rabbinic law.»
